# The us-equities pack

*US equities* · version 1.0.0 · code `USEQS`

## What it is

Public data on the companies of the Dow 30, the Nasdaq-100 and the S&P 500, and on the major US, Canadian and UK banks that file
with the SEC (three lists kept by Drishti: `IDX BANKS-US`, `IDX BANKS-CA`, `IDX BANKS-UK`): their SEC filings, ten fiscal years of
annual financials from their XBRL filings (a 10-K, or a foreign bank's 20-F or 40-F in the currency it reports in, `CURRENCY`), their
LEI, their SIC sector and the indexes and lists they belong to. Banks with no SEC filings (National Bank of Canada, Standard Chartered,
Nationwide) are not here; the `gleif` pack covers them. No index weights or
levels, no GICS and no prices are shipped: `price-history` is read live by the `us-equities-prices` connector, off by default and for
internal use only.

The documents are committed as standard test data, one snapshot per kind under `data/testdata/us-equities/<kind>/`;
`tools/drishti.py lake demo` builds them into the demo lake and the pack's Delta connector `us-equities-store` serves them, so the pack
works with the demo connector off. `samples/` keeps only a few reference documents.

## Data structures

Every kind the pack owns, read from its manifest, its samples and its Sutras: how its ids look, its fields (type, an example, what it means), its nested lists and the fields that link to other kinds. A path `A[].B` is field `B` of every element of list `A`.

### `us-company`

**US company** · mnemonic `USEQ` · read through connector `us-equities-store`.

**Id:** field `TICKER`; for example `AAPL`.

| Path | Fields |
|---|---|

| `FILINGS[]` | `ACCESSION` (string), `FORM` (string), `FILED` (date), `REPORT_DATE` (date), `DESCRIPTION` (string) |

Links: `ECONOMY` → `economy`, `FACT_IDS` → `financial-fact`, `FILING_IDS` → `filing`, `INDEX_IDS` → `index-membership`, `MARKET_WATCH` → `listed-company`, `SIC_SECTOR` → `sic-sector`.

## Screens and commands

| Command | Kind | Opens |
|---|---|---|
| `USEQ` | `us-company` | US company |
| `IDX` | `index-membership` | Index members |
| `SIC` | `sic-sector` | SIC sector |
| `EDGAR` | `filing-feed` | EDGAR filings browser |
| `FILING` | `filing` | SEC filing |
| `FACT` | `financial-fact` | Financial fact |
| `PXH` | `price-history` | Price history (live, internal use only) |
| `USEQS` | — | The pack's overview: its kinds, how many each holds, an example of each |

Examples:

| Type | Shows |
|---|---|
| `USEQ AAPL` | Apple · key facts, ten years of financials, recent filings, index memberships |
| `USEQ JPM` | JPMorgan Chase · a bank's financials |
| `IDX SP500` | S&P 500 · the members, filterable; a click opens the company beside |
| `IDX DJIA` | Dow Jones Industrial Average · thirty members |
| `IDX BANKS-CA` | Canadian banks that file with the SEC · financials in CAD |
| `SIC 3674` | Semiconductors · the companies of one SIC code by revenue |
| `SIC ALL` | Every SIC code covered, by revenue |
| `EDGAR 8-K` | The latest current reports; a click opens the filing beside |
| `FACT AAPL-REVENUE` | Apple's revenue over ten fiscal years |

Screens (Sutras):

| Sutra | Kind | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `filing-feed` | `filing-feed` | The filings browser: the latest SEC filings of the covered companies, of every form or one; a click opens a filing beside. |
| `filing` | `filing` | One SEC filing: its company, form, dates, 8-K items and its links on EDGAR (metadata only; the document stays on sec.gov). |
| `financial-fact` | `financial-fact` | One financial concept of one company (revenue, net income, assets...) over up to ten fiscal years, from its 10-K XBRL filings. |
| `index-membership` | `index-membership` | An equity index's members (Dow 30, Nasdaq-100, S&P 500) as Wikidata records them; a click opens the member's summary beside. |
| `price-history` | `price-history` | A company's quote and a year of daily prices, read live by the us-equities-prices connector: off as shipped, internal use only. |
| `sic-directory` | `sic-sector` | Every SIC code of the covered companies, by revenue, and revenue by SIC division. |
| `sic-sector` | `sic-sector` | A sector by its SIC code: its companies ranked by revenue; a click opens a company's summary beside. |
| `us-company` | `us-company` | A US listed company: key facts, ten years of annual financials, recent SEC filings and index memberships, from public data. |

## Data sources and licences

Every document names its source, retrieval date and licence in `PROVENANCE`. Filings are metadata and links only; the documents stay
on sec.gov.

| Source | Licence | Internal only | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEC EDGAR (submissions, company facts XBRL) | Public domain (US government work) | no | companies, SIC codes, filings, financial facts |
| Wikidata | CC0 | no | index membership, headquarters, founding, websites |
| GLEIF LEI records | CC0 | no | each company's LEI |
| Nasdaq Trader symbol directory | Public directory, attribution | no | the listing market |
| Yahoo Finance (us-equities-prices connector, yfinance plugin) | Terms forbid redistribution; nothing committed | yes | price-history, read live only when the connector is on |

## Enabling and dependencies

Builds on no other pack.

The connectors it brings (written once to `config/connectors/<name>.yaml`, then the site's own):

| Connector | Plugin | Kinds | Enabled |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-equities-store` | `delta` | `us-company`, `index-membership`, `sic-sector`, `filing-feed`, `filing`, `financial-fact` | `${DRISHTI_LAKE_ENABLED:true}` |
| `us-equities-prices` | `yfinance` | `price-history` | `${DRISHTI_US_EQUITIES_PRICES_ENABLED:false}` |

Settings (environment variables) its connectors read: `DRISHTI_DELTA_ROOT`, `DRISHTI_LAKE_ENABLED`, `DRISHTI_US_EQUITIES_PRICES_ENABLED`, `DRISHTI_YFINANCE_URL`.

## Refreshing the data

`python3 tools/publicdata/us_equities.py status` shows what the pack holds and how old it is; `refresh` fetches, rebuilds and checks (docs/guides/PUBLIC_DATA.md).

The pack's files are written by `tools/packgen/us_equities/make.py`; its `--check` fails when the committed files differ from what it would write.
